title: Partial & Expression Indexes
description: Shrink index sizes by 95% with Partial Indexes (WHERE) and index computed functions with Expression Indexes.

data.text: Indexes do not have to index every row or raw column. **Partial Indexes** index a subset of rows matching a predicate, while **Expression Indexes** index the computed output of functions.

data.title: Partial Index on Unprocessed Queue Items
data.content: Indexes only 0.1% of rows that actually need processing, keeping the index in RAM.

data.text: An expression index stores the result of an expression, so the query must use the exact same expression to benefit. The classic case is case-insensitive email lookup: index `lower(email)` and write `WHERE lower(email) = lower($1)`. The index works on any expression PostgreSQL can compute deterministically, including `date_trunc` and JSON path extraction.

data.title: Index the expression the query actually uses
data.content: The index matches `lower(email)`, so the lookup becomes an index scan instead of a sequential scan with a function filter.
data.code:
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_users_lower_email
ON users (lower(email));

EXPLAIN ANALYZE
SELECT id, email
FROM users
WHERE lower(email) = lower('Ada@Example.com');
-- Index Scan using ux_users_lower_email on users
--   Index Cond: (lower(email) = 'ada@example.com')

-- Partial + expression combined: only active rows, indexed by month
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_active_month
ON orders (date_trunc('month', created_at))
WHERE status = 'ACTIVE';

data.title: The expression must match exactly
data.text: PostgreSQL only uses an expression index when the query contains an expression it can prove equivalent to the indexed one. `WHERE upper(email) = ...` will not use an index on `lower(email)`. Keep the exact form in a reusable predicate or view so application code and the index do not drift apart.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Partial indexes save massive disk space and RAM by indexing only actionable rows.
Expression indexes allow SARGable queries on wrapped functions like `LOWER(email)`.
Queries must include the exact `WHERE` predicate of the partial index to utilize it.
